newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL TITLE OR BUST FOR PACKERS, SAYS FREEMAN.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL TITLE OR BUST FOR PACKERS, SAYS FREEMAN.

text.p: Getting to the Super Bowl is not good enough for the Packers, Green Bay wide receiver Antonio Freeman said Wednesday.

The Packers, making their first appearance in the National Football League championship game in 29 years, must beat the New England Patriots for the season to be a success as far as Freeman is concerned.
"The pressure has been on the Packers all year," said Freeman, one of Green Bay star quarterback Brett Favre's favourite targets. "Many people predicted us to be in the Super Bowl and here we are.
"So it's point blank. If we go in there and lose, the season is a bust. We set our sights on winning the Super Bowl."

Green Bay (15-3) is favoured by two touchdowns to beat New England (13-5) and extend the Super Bowl winning streak of National Football Conference teams to 13 in a row over their American Football Conference opponents.
Packers' coach Mike Holmgren, meanwhile, is concentrating on how to prepare his team for the January 26 Superdome showdown in New Orleans.
"We're going to have a normal week of practice and get most of our game plan in, hopefully, by Sunday," he said.
"You've got more time so you should be better prepared."
Holmgren said he would hold a few things back to give players things to work on in the second week and keep them from getting stale ahead of the hyped up title game.
"The most important thing you have to fight, in my opinion, is a certain staleness that happens with your players. There's a thin line between getting them ready and over-preparing.

"I'll put in things next week. I think it's important to challenge their minds, too, in that second week. You can't go in and just say, 'Okay, he's the script we ran last week.' That doesn't work. Not when you've got a veteran team and they're sharp and they want to be challenged."
Holmgren said ball possession figured to be a key factor for both teams.

"They have a lot of weapons on offence and a great young quarterback (Drew Bledsoe) who can throw it all over the park and a great runner (Curtis Martin)," he said. "Ideally, you want to keep their offence off the field if you can.

"In a perfect world I'd like to do that and I know Bill (Patriot coach Parcells) would like a time of possession advantage for his team. He's had that in the Super Bowls he's been in before and it's been important."
